payload.root_cause: `slugify` in src/text.js line 11 uses `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` without the global regex flag `g`. In JavaScript, `String.prototype.replace` with a non-global regex replaces only the first match, so only the first whitespace/dash run is converted to a single dash; every subsequent gap (e.g. the double space between 'Big' and 'World') is left as raw whitespace. For input 'Hello Big  World!' the pipeline yields 'hello-big  world' instead of 'hello-big-world'. The fix is to make the regex global: `/[\s-]+/g` (matching the `g` flag already correctly used on lines 10 and 12 of the same function).

payload.rationale: The root cause is that `String.prototype.replace` with a non-global regex only replaces the first match. On line 11 of src/text.js, `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` collapses only the first whitespace/dash run into a dash, leaving later gaps (e.g. the double space between 'Big' and 'World') as raw whitespace. Adding the `g` flag makes the regex global so every whitespace/dash run is replaced with a single dash, matching the `g` flag already used on the adjacent lines 10 and 12. With this change, slugify('Hello Big  World!') → 'hello-big  world' becomes 'hello-big-world', and slugify('  Already-slugged  title ') → 'already-slugged-title' as expected by the tests.
